Engine.TopUp is idempotent on a required Livepeer-Request-Id: recorded-outcome replay ahead of every other check, request_id_reuse on a different envelope, nonce-replay read as already-credited with the lease unextended, control-WS frame carrying request_id, records evicted on the job idempotency window. paid-session.md 1.0.4-draft + conformance scenario topup-replay-is-idempotent (33/33).

CreatePayment takes a required mint_request_id with durable exact-response replay in a new sender-side BoltDB ledger, surviving restart. Eviction is made safe by permanent tombstones: an evicted key is refused (FAILED_PRECONDITION), never re-minted. Namespace is the daemon's sender identity, 128-byte cap. Rotation retries documented as new intents needing new keys. --mint-retention (default 24h) sweeps payloads only.

Rebind implemented in sessionengine: declared via Livepeer-Rebind-From (and rebind_from on the WS frame), three guards with the successor-must-credit check load-bearing, predecessor settled before close, new binding persisted before the predecessor is closed, cumulative totals continuous with GenerationStartUnits marking the generation boundary, debit_seq reset per generation, bounded offerings refused, rotation chain in status, session.rebound emitted as control-plane signalling.

recipient_rotated (409) on both protocols so gateways act on a code, not a message; session.max_rotations axis (default 3) plus the zero-delivery rule that catches a rotate loop after one round; both end the session with payment_unrecoverable. Rotation chain already in status from .10.1.

Sessions now produce a settlement record built from broker state: session_id, work_id, predecessor, generation, cumulative claimed/debited with debited authoritative, one-ceiling billed value, per-generation subtotals, amount_wei + per_units for independent recomputation, settlement_seq monotonic per session, issued_at and state. Funded value accumulated cumulatively and per generation. Emitted on end and served by GET /v1/settlement/{id}, resolvable by session_id or any work_id the session has held.

settlement_keys in manifest schema 2.3.0, carried into the coordinator's signed payload by both canonical builders, verified and projected by the registry daemon onto SelectedRoute (all currently-valid keys, newest first, with windows and introducing publication_seq). Malformed delegations refused at decode.

Livepeer-Settlement is a signed JSON envelope on both protocols: JCS-canonical payload over proto field names, EIP-191 secp256k1 signature from a delegated hot key (identity.settlement_key_file), signature omitted when no key is configured. go-ethereum v1.17.2 added to the broker to match the repo's verifier. Tests cover canonical stability, recovery to the delegated key, tamper rejection, and the unsigned case.

Settlement signing complete across its three parts: sessions produce a settlement record at all (f9d646d), delegation discovery through manifest + coordinator + resolver projection (309394c), and the signed envelope on both protocols (4ef504d). LOC can verify an SDK-forwarded record against a key resolved from its own route snapshot, or bypass the SDK entirely via GET /v1/settlement/{id}.

All four landed: mint reserve-before-sign plus per-id serialization with a completed flag distinguishing expiry from an incomplete mint; job settlements carry issued_at, work_id AND job_id inside the signature (work_id alone is insufficient on paid-job); billed_value_wei ceilings via payment.BillFor. SufficientBalance is checked before the handler runs; a session that cannot cover one work unit is refused with insufficient_balance (402). debit_seq now allocated from a durable per-work_id counter (job path) and reserved on the record before debiting (session path); the broker no longer closes a shared payee session; the debit error is no longer discarded. Regression test with a negative control per defect. Verified on Arbitrum One: job 2 on a shared session now debits. A residual mismatch between the ledger's cumulative charge and the settlement's independent ceiling is filed separately.

chain-probe committed at payment-daemon/cmd/livepeer-chain-probe with a README that states the cost of a run before the command, warns to keep per_units above 1, and says to run it twice. Asserts on ledger movement and signed settlement rather than log lines, recomputing the billing rule independently of the broker. It found three defects on its first real use.

DebitBalance returns the amount charged and the cumulative unit total; both settlement paths attest that rather than recomputing. offering-axes 1.0.5-draft states the cumulative curve spans exchanges and that a settlement must attest the ledger's charge. Verified on Arbitrum One: three jobs on one session charged 5/4/4 with settlements matching exactly. Also fixed a silent no-op edit that left the charge at zero.

Added payment_cumulative_units, sourced from the ledger, distinct from the exchange/session-scoped debited_units — which the job path had been overloading with the identity's total, making one field mean two things across protocols. paid-job charges are now fully recomputable from a record; paid-session charges on a shared identity are attested rather than recomputable, and offering-axes 1.0.6-draft says so.
